statement: A test that a batched or paged read equals the one-shot read is only as strong as its fixture. Each split point must be crossed, and each split read must be the only source of some finding. Cejel #572 re-runs A2's history reads in rev-list pages of 50,000 commits and in batches of 1,000. Its equality test used a 17-commit fixture, so no page boundary was ever crossed, and every finding was found by two readers. Review mutants survived: a one-commit gap between pages, reading only the first page, and parsing only the first batch of the tree enumeration. Each would have dropped history without a scan limitation, so the report would claim a complete read. A first fix put the secret in the last commit of the second page, and the gap mutant still survived. Rules: build a fixture past each real split size; put the only evidence in the first item after each boundary; give each split reader a finding no other reader supplies; show the named mutants fail.
